personas.label: Business Users

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Tableau Desktop Foundations Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The Tableau Desktop Foundations exam is the easiest Tableau certification. It tests foundational knowledge of Tableau Desktop features rather than advanced calculations or architecture, making it accessible to candidates with a few weeks of focused practice.
bullets: 40 questions in 60 minutes — 90 seconds per question, which is comfortable for candidates familiar with the Tableau Desktop interface.
~65% passing score — you need approximately 26 correct answers out of 40 to pass.
Breadth over depth — the exam covers data connections, chart types, filters, basic calculations, and dashboards, so you need working knowledge across all areas.
Two to four weeks of daily practice is typically enough — candidates with basic data literacy who practice in Tableau Desktop using sample data (like Superstore) are well prepared.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Book when you can connect to data, build common chart types, apply filters, write basic calculated fields, and create a multi-sheet dashboard without following a tutorial.

examFormat.heading: Tableau Desktop Foundations Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or in-person. Here is the format:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Questions describe a task — build a bar chart, apply a filter, create a calculated field — and ask you to identify the correct Tableau Desktop steps or feature.
bestWayToPass: Show Me panel: Know which chart type Tableau recommends for each combination of dimensions and measures, and when to override it.
Marks card: Understand how Color, Size, Label, Detail, and Tooltip encode data on marks and how changing them affects the view.
Filters and sorting: Practice applying dimension filters, measure filters, and date filters, and sorting by field value, manual drag, or nested sort.
Build a dashboard: Create a multi-sheet dashboard with Filter Actions and Highlight Actions to understand interactivity and layout containers.

certificationCard.description: Tableau Desktop Foundations validates core skills in connecting to data, building views, and creating dashboards using Tableau Desktop. It is an entry-level credential for analytics and visualization.

keyConcepts.h2: Tableau Desktop Foundations: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Connecting to Data and Data Source Basics
blocks.body: **Tableau Desktop** connects to hundreds of data sources: files (Excel, CSV, JSON), databases (SQL Server, PostgreSQL, BigQuery), and cloud services. Data Source page: connect, join or union tables, preview data, rename fields, hide unused fields, change data types. Live connection queries the database each time; Extract (.hyper) snapshots the data for performance. Field types: Dimensions (qualitative, blue), Measures (quantitative, green). Discrete fields create headers; Continuous fields create axes. Understanding pills (fields), shelves (rows, columns, marks card) and how they map to the view is the foundation of the Foundations exam.

blocks.heading: Building Basic Visualisations
blocks.body: Tableau's Show Me panel suggests chart types based on selected fields. Common charts: Bar (compare categories), Line (trend over time), Scatter (correlation between two measures), Map (geographic data), Pie (part-to-whole — use sparingly). Shelves: Columns shelf = X axis, Rows shelf = Y axis, Marks card controls colour, size, shape, label, detail, tooltip. Sorting: by field value (ascending/descending), by manual drag, or by nested sort. The Foundations exam tests how to build each chart type and which is most appropriate for a given question.

blocks.heading: Filtering, Sorting, and Groups
blocks.body: Filter types: Dimension filters (categorical), Measure filters (range/conditional), Date filters (relative, range, discrete). Filter order of operations: Extract → Data Source → Context → Dimension → Measure. Context filters improve performance by reducing the data set before other filters apply. Sets are named subsets of dimension members — In/Out members can be used in calculations. Groups combine dimension members into named categories directly on the field (e.g., combining East and West into 'Combined'). Quick filters show filter controls in the view for user interactivity.

blocks.heading: Calculated Fields: Basic Formulas
blocks.body: **calculated fields** create new data from existing fields. Basic functions: String (LEFT, RIGHT, MID, CONTAINS, LEN), Date (DATEPART, DATEDIFF, DATEADD, TODAY), Logical (IF/ELSEIF/END, IIF, CASE), Aggregate (SUM, AVG, MAX, MIN, COUNTD). **table calculations** reference values relative to other rows in the view (RUNNING_SUM, WINDOW_SUM, RANK, PREVIOUS_VALUE). The Foundations exam tests writing basic calculated fields to answer common business questions — e.g., profit margin (SUM([Profit])/SUM([Sales])), year-over-year growth, conditional categorisation.

blocks.heading: Dashboards and Stories
blocks.body: Dashboards combine multiple sheets into a single view. Layout: Tiled vs Floating objects. Containers (Horizontal, Vertical) control how objects resize together. Device preview shows how the dashboard looks on desktop, tablet, and phone. Dashboard Actions enable interactivity — Filter Action (click to filter), Highlight Action (click to highlight), URL Action (open a link). Stories are a presentation format — a sequence of Story Points, each showing a sheet or dashboard with a caption, for guided data narration. The Foundations exam tests how to create a dashboard, add interactivity, and build a basic story.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Tableau Desktop Specialist Exam
scenarioTips.intro: The Tableau Desktop Specialist exam tests foundational Tableau Desktop skills. Focus on connecting to data, building basic visualizations, and using core features. This is a practical knowledge exam — understand the UI and feature capabilities.

blocks.heading: Connecting to Data
blocks.body: Know how to connect to file-based sources (Excel, CSV, JSON), database sources, and how to configure joins and unions in the Data Source pane. Understand the difference between live and extract connections.

blocks.heading: Building Basic Visualizations
blocks.body: Know the Show Me panel chart types and when Tableau recommends each. Understand how to use Rows/Columns shelf, Marks card (color, size, label, detail, tooltip), and filters pane.

blocks.heading: Sorting & Grouping
blocks.body: Know how to sort data (field sort, manual sort, nested sort) and how to create groups (custom groups from dimension members) and sets (dynamic or fixed subsets of dimension members).

blocks.heading: Basic Calculations
blocks.body: Know how to create simple **calculated fields**: string functions (LEFT, MID, CONTAINS), date functions (DATEDIFF, DATEPART), and aggregate functions (SUM, AVG, COUNT, COUNTD) applied to measures.

blocks.heading: Sharing & Publishing
blocks.body: Know how to publish workbooks and data sources to **Tableau Server** or Cloud, export views to images/PDFs/PowerPoint, and use Tableau Reader for offline sharing.

sampleQuestions.question: What does the Tableau Desktop Foundations certification validate?
options: Core Tableau Desktop skills: connecting to data, building views, and creating dashboards
sampleQuestions.explanation: Tableau Desktop Foundations validates core skills in connecting to data, building views, and creating dashboards in Tableau Desktop.
whyWrong: 'Server administration only' misrepresents Foundations, which is about core Desktop skills, not server administration.
Marketing automation is unrelated to Tableau Desktop Foundations.
Salesforce CRM configuration is unrelated to Tableau Desktop Foundations.

sampleQuestions.question: Which is a fundamental Tableau Desktop concept?
options: Dimensions, measures, and the shelf (Rows, Columns, Marks)
sampleQuestions.explanation: Dimensions, measures, and the shelf (Rows, Columns, Marks) are fundamental to building views in Tableau Desktop.
whyWrong: 'Only colors' undersells the fundamental concepts, which include dimensions, measures, and shelves broadly.
Apex programming is a Salesforce Core language, unrelated to Tableau Desktop concepts.
Email templates are unrelated to Tableau Desktop's core visualization concepts.

sampleQuestions.question: What do the Rows and Columns shelves do in Tableau?
options: Define the structure of the view; fields placed here create headers and axes
sampleQuestions.explanation: Rows and Columns define the layout of the visualization. Fields create headers, axes, and panes.
whyWrong: 'Store data only' misrepresents the Rows/Columns shelves, which define view structure, not data storage.
'Apply filters only' undersells the Rows/Columns shelves' broader structural role beyond filtering.
'Change colors' misattributes the Rows/Columns shelves' function to a different visual property (that's the Marks card).

sampleQuestions.question: Which data type appears as a dimension (blue pill) by default in Tableau?
options: Text, dates, and booleans are typically dimensions
sampleQuestions.explanation: Text, dates, and booleans default to dimensions. Numeric fields often default to measures.
whyWrong: 'Only numbers' is the opposite of what typically becomes a dimension — numbers are usually measures.
'Only dates' undersells the broader set of data types (text, booleans too) that appear as dimensions.
'Only booleans' undersells the broader set of data types (text, dates too) that appear as dimensions.

sampleQuestions.question: What does the Marks card control in Tableau?
options: Color, size, text, detail, and tooltip of marks in the view
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Marks card controls how data points are encoded: color, size, label, tooltip, and more.
whyWrong: Data connection is a separate step, not what the Marks card itself controls.
'Filters only' undersells the Marks card's broader control over color, size, text, and detail.
'Calculations only' misattributes the Marks card's function to a different Tableau capability.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Tableau feature lets you connect to Excel or CSV files?
options: Connect to a File supports Excel, CSV, PDF, and other file types
sampleQuestions.explanation: Connect to a File lets you use Excel, CSV, and other file-based data sources.
whyWrong: 'Only databases' undersells the file-connection capability, which covers Excel, CSV, PDF, and more.
'Only PDF' undersells the broader set of file types Tableau can connect to.
'Only JSON' undersells the broader set of file types Tableau can connect to.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a filter in Tableau used for?
options: Limiting which data appears in the view based on criteria
sampleQuestions.explanation: Filters restrict the data displayed in a view based on field values or conditions.
whyWrong: 'Changing colors only' misattributes filtering's actual purpose, which is limiting displayed data.
Filters don't delete data — they limit what's displayed, not what's stored.
'Connecting to servers' misattributes filtering's function to a different, unrelated data-connection concept.

sampleQuestions.question: Which chart type uses bars to compare categories?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Bar charts compare values across categories using horizontal or vertical bars.
whyWrong: A line chart shows trends over time, not category comparison via bars.
A pie chart shows part-to-whole composition, not the bar-based category comparison being asked about.
A map shows geographic data, not the bar-based category comparison being asked about.

sampleQuestions.question: What does 'aggregate' mean in Tableau?
options: Summarize measure values (e.g., SUM, AVG) at the level of the view
sampleQuestions.explanation: Aggregation summarizes measures (SUM, AVG, etc.) at the granularity defined by dimensions in the view.
whyWrong: 'Combine colors' misattributes aggregation's function to an unrelated visual property.
Aggregation doesn't delete data — it summarizes values, not removes them.
'Connect tables' misattributes aggregation's function to a data-connection concept, which is unrelated.

sampleQuestions.question: How do you create a dashboard in Tableau Desktop?
options: Use the Dashboard tab to add worksheets and objects to a single layout
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Dashboard tab lets you add worksheets, images, text, and objects to create a unified view.
whyWrong: 'Only in Server' contradicts the fact that dashboards are built directly in Tableau Desktop.
'Dashboards are automatic' contradicts the fact that building a dashboard requires deliberate use of the Dashboard tab.
'Only from CSV' incorrectly ties dashboard creation to a specific data source type, which isn't a requirement.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the difference between discrete and continuous in Tableau?
options: Discrete creates headers; continuous creates axes. Blue = discrete, green = continuous
sampleQuestions.explanation: Discrete fields create headers and categories; continuous fields create axes. Pill color indicates type.
whyWrong: 'No difference' contradicts the fact that discrete and continuous have distinct, defined behaviors (headers vs. axes).
'Only for colors' undersells the broader header-versus-axis distinction discrete/continuous represents.
'Only for dates' undersells the broader applicability of the discrete/continuous distinction beyond just dates.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Tableau feature shows a summary when you hover over a mark?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Tooltips display contextual information when users hover over marks in the view.
whyWrong: Filters limit displayed data — they don't show a hover summary.
Legends explain color/size encoding — they don't show a hover summary of a specific mark.
Parameters are input controls — they don't show a hover summary of a mark.

sampleQuestions.question: What does the Show Me panel in Tableau do?
options: Recommends chart types based on selected fields
sampleQuestions.explanation: Show Me suggests visualization types based on the fields you have selected.
whyWrong: 'Manages licenses' misattributes Show Me's function to an unrelated administrative feature.
'Connects to data only' misattributes Show Me's function, which is chart recommendation, not data connection.
'Applies filters only' misattributes Show Me's function to a different, unrelated feature.

sampleQuestions.question: How do you sort a bar chart in Tableau?
options: Click the sort icon on the axis or use the sort option in the field menu
sampleQuestions.explanation: Use the sort icon on the axis or the field's sort option to order bars by value or manually.
whyWrong: 'Cannot sort' contradicts the fact that sorting is a standard, available Tableau feature.
Sorting isn't limited to dashboards — it's available directly on worksheets too.
Sorting isn't limited to dimensions — measures can be involved in sort order too.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Tableau worksheet?
options: A single visualization (chart, map, or table) built from data
sampleQuestions.explanation: A worksheet is a single view—one chart, map, or table. Dashboards combine multiple worksheets.
whyWrong: A data source is the underlying connection, not the visualization itself.
A dashboard combines multiple worksheets — a single worksheet is a smaller, individual component.
A filter limits displayed data — it isn't itself a visualization.
